component.name: Safeer Browser
component.summary: Sovereign, fast and private WebKit web browser

description.p: Safeer Browser is an open-source, sovereign, and lightweight web browser natively engineered with GTK3 and WebKit2GTK for Linux Mint (Cinnamon, MATE, XFCE) and Ubuntu. It provides bookmarks, configurable privacy settings and a desktop interface.
Key Highlights:

ul.li: YouTube playback and configurable ad filtering.
Local reverse domain trie threat shield blocking botnets, ransomware and phishing, from signed lists (sources include abuse.ch, Phishing Army and SI-CERT).
Instant 1-click bookmarks import directly from Firefox and Chrome profiles.
Onboarding wizard with DuckDuckGo default search and optional default browser setting.
Bookmarks toolbar and muscle-memory keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+Shift+T, Ctrl+Tab, Ctrl+K).
Encrypted DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) local loopback tunnel and strict 3rd-party cookie blocking.
Native Debian package (.deb) with safe alternatives priority (40) that never aggressively hijacks defaults.

description.p: Safeer Browser: the Safeer Link page names devices for everyone (the name is kept by Safeer Link). Safeer Control 2.0.9: "Connect a new device" shows a code that any phone opens in its browser - no Safeer app needed (Safeer Link Web); devices can be renamed from the computer and the name is shown the same on every device. New package safeer-os 0.4.1: Safeer OS for Linux - programs, files, devices, network, sound and Shield in one full-screen shell over Linux Mint, also as AppImage and Flatpak with Safeer Control included.

Safeer Browser: no functional changes. Safeer Control 2.0.8: leftover Safeer-TV sound outputs are removed, so sound over HDMI keeps working after using Safeer Link; the Safeer-TV output now exists only while a program started from the TV is running.

Safeer Browser: no functional changes. Safeer Control 2.0.7: the selection frame and clicks on the TV are exact also in GTK4 programs, dialogs start on their default button and pages scroll at the edge; the separate TV screen has no tab bar, and its programs close when the TV session ends or the TV disappears.

Safeer Browser: no functional changes. Safeer Control 2.0.6: on the separate TV screen a short press of the remote's arrow jumps to the next button, link or field, like on Android, and holding it moves the pointer freely; this also works in Brave, Chrome and other Chromium browsers. Ending the session on the TV closes the programs it started on the computer.

Safeer Browser: no functional changes. Safeer Control 2.0.5 (separate package safeer-control): programs started from Safeer OS on your TV open on a separate, invisible screen instead of on your desktop, so your monitor, mouse and keyboard stay yours; the TV shows and controls only that screen and its sound plays on the TV. The package installs sway, wf-recorder and wtype for this itself, and if one is missing later or wf-recorder is too old, Safeer Control offers to install or update it when you click and confirm. Games from the TV start in key mode, and in other programs the controller's D-pad jumps between buttons and fields. Programs can be closed from the TV, and when the last one closes the TV returns to Safeer OS instead of showing a dark screen.

Safeer Browser now speaks your language: the settings window, its dialogs and the home page follow the system language in English, Slovenian, German, Spanish, French and Italian, instead of showing parts of the interface in Slovenian only. The project is now public, with an English README, a contributing guide and a code of conduct. Safeer Control is unchanged (2.0.2).

Safeer Browser: no functional changes. Safeer Control 2.0.2 (separate package safeer-control): shows your computer's programs on the TV sorted into groups (games, office, web, media, programming, learning, tools) with search by name; a key held on the remote is now really held on the computer, so games and long scrolling work; icons of apps installed for your user only (flatpak --user) are found. Fixed: the installed Safeer Control failed to start because three modules were missing from the package.

Safeer Browser: no functional changes. Safeer Control 2.0.1 (separate package safeer-control): runs quietly in the background with a tray icon and starts at login after the first pairing; shares folders you pick with Safeer OS on your TV, which plays films, music and photos straight from this computer over the home network.

Safeer Link: the remote shows which device is the Safeer Link hub and whose apps it lists; the Menu key opens the menu on the TV or phone and the remote's keys then move inside that menu; the home page is no longer offered for sending; a pairing the hub no longer knows leads to a new pairing instead of endless connecting. The Safeer Link window shows the right state as soon as it opens. New: Safeer Control, a standalone desktop app with Safeer Link built in (separate package safeer-control), which takes over this browser's pairing without a new code.

Safeer Link: control your TV from this computer. Click the TV in the Safeer Link window and choose Remote: keys, volume, the TV's apps and a screenshot of its screen; type a command, a page or a search. Your phone or TV can control this computer's Safeer the same way (open pages, scroll, play or pause, volume).
Safeer Link: give your devices your own names, kept on this computer only; the name is used in the device list, when sending a page and in notifications.

PDF files on your computer open in Safeer: choose "Open with Safeer" in the file manager or enter a file:// address. Safeer Link texts no longer use the word "hub": start on any device, the others join.
Saving from the built-in PDF viewer works again and keeps the document's file name; downloads that web pages generate in the browser (for example exported CSV files) are no longer blocked.
The built-in PDF viewer follows the language chosen in Safeer instead of the system language, and a tab showing a PDF is named after the file.

Safeer Link: any device can be the hub, so no TV is required; when the hub goes away the computer finds another one and reconnects without a new code if already paired. The computer sends text, files and its screen to any device and receives pages, text, files and screens from any device, also in the background. All connections are encrypted (TLS) and bound to the hub key; the pairing code never travels over the network. The DNS-over-HTTPS proxy no longer refuses private network addresses.

Copying a link out of the address bar works as it should: the full address is in place before the cursor moves, a drag selection is left exactly as you made it, copying the whole address puts the real, complete link on the clipboard, scheme included, and right-clicking the address bar or a bookmark offers "Copy link". Text typed into the address bar is no longer overwritten when you return to the window.

"Set as default browser" works again on every install: a leftover launcher entry from an older Safeer install is repaired or retired, paths are quoted only where the specification requires it so xdg-open honours the choice, the packaged entry names the launcher by its full path, and a failure can no longer take the window down.

One page can no longer take the computer down: every tab has its own memory limit (half of RAM, so no normal page reaches it) and only a runaway page is stopped, with a notice; the browser watches each tab's CPU and memory, marks a heavy tab with a 🔥 and a menu, puts a heavy background tab without sound to sleep after a minute, and offers a task manager at safeer://procesi. The periodic page scripts run only when the browser is idle and never in hidden tabs; the browser runs in its own user cgroup scope and keeps a log in ~/.config/safeer-mint/safeer.log.

YouTube and YouTube Music no longer stop with "Video paused. Continue watching?": while media plays, the browser reports activity through YouTube's own activity signal, which cancels the scheduled prompt and pause; the dialog is also recognised and confirmed on its own if it ever appears.

Fewer ads: the full EasyList ad list is compiled into a WebKit content filter and refreshed in the background, so ad requests are stopped in the network layer without slowing pages. Fake bank pages opened from a local HTML attachment get the same warning as a look-alike address, pages asking for a card number under the guise of a fine or parcel fee are stopped as a card trap, and tax-number and PIN fields count as credentials.

Protection against web traps updated: warnings for fake online banks with a link to the real bank, real banks and payment pages work undisturbed, and threat lists are loaded and checked in the background after every start. Links for installed programs (such as the return to the Claude app after signing in) open after confirmation, and YouTube no longer pauses with "Continue watching?".
YouTube Music keeps playing in a minimized or background window: user activity stays current without timers and the idle prompt is confirmed immediately.
Hide empty ad inserts and "Please disable adblock or subscribe" placeholders on Push Square, Nintendo Life, Pure Xbox and Time Extension.
YouTube and YouTube Music keep playing without the "Video paused. Continue watching?" prompt.
Keep WebKit finalization on the GTK thread, prevent crash reload loops and defer restored background tabs.
Linux packaging and desktop appearance improvements.
Preserve Grok sign-in pages, use native WebKit identity, and retain YouTube playback configuration.
Reduce redundant YouTube page work and use the web browser resource cache.
More stable video playback and safe recovery from interrupted search connections.
Fix default browser registration and verification.
Preserve sign-in popups, forms and verification pages.
Fix startup with enabled sidebar integrations.
Fix encrypted DNS transport, concurrent connections, YouTube media stability and false malware warnings for advertising domains.

Release v1.0.7: Added onboarding setup wizard, bookmarks toolbar, DuckDuckGo default search engine, keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+Shift+T, Ctrl+Tab, Ctrl+1..9, Ctrl+K), and safe alternatives priority (40).
Release v1.0.6: 1-click bookmarks import from Firefox and Chrome, session restore, Ctrl+F in-page search, Ctrl+P print to PDF, and DoH proxy.
